chapters.title: Parts of Speech
chapters.intro: Every English word belongs to one of eight parts of speech, decided by the job it does in a sentence.
chapters.introBn: ইংরেজির প্রতিটি শব্দ বাক্যে তার কাজ অনুযায়ী আটটি Parts of Speech-এর একটিতে পড়ে।

lessons.heading: Noun (বিশেষ্য)
lessons.body: A noun names a person, place, thing, animal or idea.
lessons.bodyBn: ব্যক্তি, স্থান, বস্তু বা ভাবের নাম।

lessons.heading: Pronoun (সর্বনাম)
lessons.body: A pronoun is used instead of a noun.

lessons.heading: Verb (ক্রিয়া)
lessons.body: A verb expresses an action or a state of being.

lessons.heading: Adjective (বিশেষণ)
lessons.body: An adjective describes or qualifies a noun or pronoun.
lessons.bodyBn: বিশেষ্য বা সর্বনামের দোষ-গুণ প্রকাশ করে।

lessons.heading: Adverb (ক্রিয়া-বিশেষণ)
lessons.body: An adverb modifies a verb, adjective or another adverb.
lessons.bodyBn: ক্রিয়া, বিশেষণ বা অন্য adverb-কে বিশেষিত করে।

lessons.heading: Preposition (পদান্বয়ী অব্যয়)
lessons.body: A preposition shows the relation of a noun/pronoun to another word.
lessons.bodyBn: বিশেষ্য/সর্বনামের সাথে অন্য শব্দের সম্পর্ক বোঝায়।
examples: The book is on the table.

lessons.heading: Conjunction (সংযোজক অব্যয়)
lessons.body: A conjunction joins words, phrases or clauses.
lessons.bodyBn: শব্দ, বাক্যাংশ বা বাক্যকে যুক্ত করে।

lessons.heading: Interjection (আবেগসূচক অব্যয়)
lessons.body: An interjection expresses sudden emotion.

quiz.q: What part of speech is the underlined word: 'He runs QUICKLY.'
quiz.explain: 'Quickly' tells how he runs, so it modifies the verb — it is an adverb.

quiz.q: Identify the noun: 'Dhaka is a big city.'
quiz.explain: 'Dhaka' names a place, so it is a noun.

quiz.q: Which word is a conjunction? 'He is poor but honest.'
quiz.explain: 'But' joins two ideas, so it is a conjunction.

quiz.q: 'WOW! What a beautiful scene.' — 'Wow' is a/an:
quiz.explain: It expresses sudden emotion — an interjection.

quiz.q: Identify the pronoun: 'They play football.'
quiz.explain: 'They' stands for a noun, so it is a pronoun.

quiz.q: What part of speech is 'on' in 'The cat is on the roof.'?
quiz.explain: 'On' shows position/relation — a preposition.

chapters.title: Tenses
chapters.intro: Tense shows the time of an action. There are three main tenses — present, past and future — each with four forms.
chapters.introBn: Tense ক্রিয়ার সময় বোঝায়। প্রধান তিনটি কাল — present, past, future — প্রতিটির চারটি রূপ আছে।

lessons.heading: Present Tense
lessons.body: Simple (I eat), Continuous (I am eating), Perfect (I have eaten), Perfect Continuous (I have been eating).
examples: She goes to school every day.

lessons.heading: Past Tense
lessons.body: Simple (I ate), Continuous (I was eating), Perfect (I had eaten), Perfect Continuous (I had been eating).
examples: We were reading when he called.
She had left before I arrived.

lessons.heading: Future Tense
lessons.body: Simple (I shall/will eat), Continuous (I will be eating), Perfect (I will have eaten), Perfect Continuous (I will have been eating).

lessons.heading: Signal words (সংকেত শব্দ)
lessons.body: every day, usually -> Simple Present; now, at present -> Present Continuous; already, just, yet -> Present Perfect; yesterday, ago -> Simple Past; tomorrow -> Future.
lessons.bodyBn: এই শব্দগুলো দেখে সঠিক tense চেনা যায়।
examples: I met him two days AGO.

quiz.q: She ____ to school every day.
quiz.explain: 'Every day' signals a habit -> Simple Present, and the subject 'she' takes 'goes'.

quiz.q: Look! The baby ____ .
quiz.explain: 'Look!' shows an action happening now -> Present Continuous.

quiz.q: I ____ my lunch already.
quiz.explain: 'Already' signals Present Perfect.

quiz.q: He ____ the work before I came.
quiz.explain: An earlier past action before another past -> Past Perfect.

quiz.q: We ____ him tomorrow.
quiz.explain: 'Tomorrow' signals the future -> 'will meet'.

quiz.q: They ____ football when it started to rain.
quiz.explain: An ongoing past action interrupted by another -> Past Continuous.

chapters.title: Active & Passive Voice
chapters.intro: Voice shows whether the subject does the action (Active) or receives it (Passive).
chapters.introBn: Voice বোঝায় subject নিজে কাজ করে (Active) নাকি কাজটি ভোগ করে (Passive)।

lessons.heading: The basic idea
lessons.body: Active: Subject + Verb + Object. Passive: Object + be + past participle (V3) + by + Subject.
examples: Passive: Rice is eaten by Rahim.

lessons.heading: Steps to change
lessons.body: 1) Object becomes the subject. 2) Use the right form of 'be' + V3. 3) Put the old subject after 'by'.
lessons.bodyBn: Object আগে, be + V3, তারপর by + কর্তা।
examples: Passive: A letter was written by her.

lessons.heading: 'be' by tense
lessons.body: Simple Present -> is/am/are; Present Continuous -> is/am/are being; Past -> was/were; Present Perfect -> has/have been; Future -> will be.
examples: Passive (cont.): The work is being done.
Passive (perfect): The work has been done.

lessons.heading: Questions & imperatives
lessons.body: Interrogative: keep the question form. Imperative: 'Let + object + be + V3'.
examples: Active: Do it now. Passive: Let it be done now.
Active: Who broke the glass? Passive: By whom was the glass broken?

quiz.q: Passive of 'Rahim eats rice.'
quiz.explain: Simple Present passive -> is/am/are + V3: 'is eaten'.

quiz.q: Passive of 'She is writing a letter.'
options: A letter is written by her.
A letter is being written by her.
A letter was written by her.
A letter being written by her.
quiz.explain: Present Continuous passive -> is being + V3.

quiz.q: Passive of 'Do the work.'
quiz.explain: Imperative passive -> 'Let + object + be + V3'.

quiz.q: Active of 'The thief was caught by the police.'
options: The police has caught the thief.
quiz.explain: 'was ... by' is Past passive -> active Simple Past 'caught'.

quiz.q: Passive of 'They have finished the project.'
quiz.explain: Present Perfect passive -> has/have been + V3.

quiz.q: Choose the correct passive: 'Who wrote this poem?'
options: By whom was this poem written?
quiz.explain: Past passive of a 'who' question -> 'By whom was ... written?'

chapters.title: Narration (Direct & Indirect)
chapters.intro: Narration is reporting someone's words — either the exact words (Direct) or in our own words (Indirect).
chapters.introBn: কারও কথা বলা — হুবহু (Direct) অথবা নিজের ভাষায় (Indirect)।

lessons.heading: Direct vs Indirect
lessons.body: Direct keeps the exact words inside quotation marks. Indirect reports them without quotation marks.
lessons.bodyBn: Direct-এ inverted comma থাকে, Indirect-এ থাকে না।
examples: Indirect: He said that he was ill.

lessons.heading: Key changes
lessons.body: 1) Reporting verb may change (say to/tell, ask, order, request). 2) Use a linker (that / if / to). 3) Change pronouns to suit the speaker. 4) Back-shift the tense if the reporting verb is past.
lessons.bodyBn: Pronoun, tense ও সময়-স্থানবাচক শব্দ বদলায়।
examples: now -> then, today -> that day, here -> there, this -> that, ago -> before

lessons.heading: Sentence types
lessons.body: Assertive: say/tell + that. Interrogative: ask + if/whether (or wh-word), change to statement order. Imperative: tell/order/request/advise + to + verb.
examples: Direct: He said to me, 'Are you happy?' -> Indirect: He asked me if I was happy.
Direct: He said to me, 'Go away.' -> Indirect: He ordered me to go away.

lessons.heading: Optative & Exclamatory
lessons.body: Use 'wish/pray' for optative; 'exclaim with joy/sorrow that' for exclamatory.
examples: Direct: He said, 'May you live long!' -> Indirect: He prayed that I might live long.

quiz.q: Indirect: He said, 'I am happy.'
options: He said that he is happy.
He said that he was happy.
quiz.explain: Past reporting verb back-shifts 'am' to 'was'; 'I' becomes 'he'.

quiz.q: Indirect: She said to me, 'Are you ready?'
options: She asked me if I was ready.
She said that I was ready.
She asked me that I am ready.
She told me if I am ready.
quiz.explain: Yes/no question -> ask + if + statement order, tense back-shifts.

quiz.q: Indirect: He said to me, 'Please help me.'
options: He requested me to help him.
quiz.explain: 'Please' + command -> request + to + verb; pronoun changes.

quiz.q: 'now' in indirect speech (past) becomes:
quiz.explain: Time word change: now -> then.

quiz.q: Indirect: The teacher said, 'The earth moves round the sun.'
options: said that the earth moves round the sun
quiz.explain: A universal truth does NOT change tense.

quiz.q: Indirect: He said, 'What a nice bird!'
options: He said the bird is nice.
He exclaimed with joy that it was a very nice bird.
He asked what a nice bird.
quiz.explain: Exclamatory -> 'exclaimed with joy that ...'

chapters.title: Sentence Transformation
chapters.intro: Transformation changes the FORM of a sentence while keeping the same MEANING.
chapters.introBn: অর্থ ঠিক রেখে বাক্যের গঠন পরিবর্তন করা।

lessons.heading: Simple, Complex, Compound
lessons.body: Simple: one clause. Complex: one main + one or more subordinate clause (with because, although, that, if...). Compound: two main clauses joined by and, but, so, or.
lessons.bodyBn: একটি clause -> Simple; main+sub -> Complex; দুটি main -> Compound।
examples: Simple: Being ill, he could not come.
Complex: As he was ill, he could not come.
Compound: He was ill and could not come.

lessons.heading: Affirmative <-> Negative
lessons.body: Keep the meaning by using opposite words: only/alone -> none but; must -> cannot but; every -> there is no ... that ... not.
examples: Aff: Only Allah can help us.
Neg: None but Allah can help us.

lessons.heading: Assertive <-> Interrogative
lessons.body: Turn a statement into a question that means the same: 'Everybody loves flowers.' -> 'Who does not love flowers?'
examples: Assertive: It is no use crying.
Interrogative: What is the use of crying?

lessons.heading: Degree (Positive/Comparative/Superlative)
lessons.body: No other ... as ... as (positive); ...-er than any other (comparative); the ...-est (superlative).
examples: Superlative: Dhaka is the biggest city in Bangladesh.
Comparative: Dhaka is bigger than any other city in Bangladesh.
Positive: No other city in Bangladesh is as big as Dhaka.

quiz.q: Make negative: 'Only Allah can save us.'
options: None but Allah can save us.
quiz.explain: 'Only' (a person) -> 'None but' keeps the meaning.

quiz.q: Complex form of 'Being ill, he could not come.'
options: He was ill and could not come.
As he was ill, he could not come.
He could not come for illness.
quiz.explain: Adding the subordinate clause 'As he was ill' makes it complex.

quiz.q: Comparative of 'Dhaka is the biggest city in Bangladesh.'
options: Dhaka is bigger than any other city in Bangladesh.
No city is big as Dhaka.
quiz.explain: Superlative -> comparative: '...-er than any other ...'.

quiz.q: Interrogative of 'Everybody wants to be happy.'
options: Who does not want to be happy?
quiz.explain: Affirmative-assertive -> negative-interrogative keeps the meaning.

quiz.q: Compound form of 'As he is honest, he is loved by all.'
options: He is honest and is loved by all.
quiz.explain: Two main clauses joined by 'and' -> compound.

quiz.q: Simple form of 'When the sun rose, the fog disappeared.'
options: The sun rose and fog gone.
quiz.explain: Reducing the clause to a phrase 'At sunrise' makes it a simple sentence.

chapters.title: Modal Verbs
chapters.intro: Modal verbs (can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, ought to) are helping verbs that express ability, permission, possibility, obligation, advice and more.
chapters.introBn: Modal verb দিয়ে সামর্থ্য, অনুমতি, সম্ভাবনা, বাধ্যবাধকতা ও উপদেশ বোঝানো হয়।

lessons.heading: can / could
lessons.body: can -> present ability or permission; could -> past ability or polite request.
lessons.bodyBn: সামর্থ্য/অনুমতি; could অতীত বা ভদ্র অনুরোধ।

lessons.heading: may / might
lessons.body: may -> permission or possibility; might -> weaker possibility or wish.

lessons.heading: shall / should
lessons.body: should -> advice, duty or suggestion (ought to).

lessons.heading: must / have to / ought to
lessons.body: must -> strong obligation or certainty; have to -> necessity; ought to -> moral duty.
examples: We ought to help the poor.

lessons.heading: will / would
lessons.body: will -> future or willingness; would -> polite request, past habit or condition.
lessons.bodyBn: will -> ভবিষ্যৎ; would -> ভদ্র অনুরোধ/অতীত অভ্যাস।
examples: Would you mind closing the door?

quiz.q: ____ you help me, please? (polite request)
quiz.explain: 'Could' makes a polite request.

quiz.q: You ____ respect your parents. (advice/duty)
quiz.explain: 'Should' gives advice or expresses duty.

quiz.q: It ____ rain today; take an umbrella. (possibility)
quiz.explain: 'May' expresses possibility.

quiz.q: Every citizen ____ obey the law. (strong obligation)
quiz.explain: 'Must' expresses strong obligation.

quiz.q: I ____ swim when I was five. (past ability)
quiz.explain: 'Could' expresses past ability.

quiz.q: We ____ help the helpless. (moral duty)
quiz.explain: 'Ought to' expresses moral duty.

chapters.title: Articles (a, an, the)
chapters.intro: Articles come before nouns. 'a' and 'an' are indefinite; 'the' is definite.
chapters.introBn: Article বিশেষ্যের আগে বসে। a/an অনির্দিষ্ট, the নির্দিষ্ট।

lessons.heading: a vs an (by SOUND)
lessons.body: Use 'a' before a consonant sound, 'an' before a vowel sound — judge by sound, not spelling.

lessons.heading: the (definite)
lessons.body: Use 'the' for something specific or already mentioned, unique things, superlatives, rivers/seas, and nationalities.
examples: the sun, the Padma, the best student

lessons.heading: Zero article (no article)
lessons.body: Use no article before proper nouns, languages, meals, and general plural/uncountable nouns.
lessons.bodyBn: ভাষা, খাবার, সাধারণ অর্থে article বসে না।

quiz.q: He is ____ university student.
quiz.explain: 'University' starts with a 'yu' consonant sound -> 'a'.

quiz.q: I waited for ____ hour.
quiz.explain: 'Hour' has a silent 'h' (vowel sound) -> 'an'.

quiz.q: ____ Padma is a big river.
quiz.explain: Rivers take 'the'.

quiz.q: He is ____ best boy in the class.
quiz.explain: Superlatives take 'the'.

quiz.q: She speaks ____ English fluently.
quiz.explain: Names of languages take no article.

quiz.q: I bought ____ honest man's book — he is ____ MP.
quiz.explain: 'honest' (silent h) and 'MP' (em- vowel sound) both take 'an'.

chapters.title: Subject-Verb Agreement
chapters.intro: A verb must agree with its subject in number and person.
chapters.introBn: Verb তার subject-এর সাথে number ও person-এ মিল রাখে।

lessons.heading: Number agreement
lessons.body: A singular subject takes a singular verb; a plural subject takes a plural verb.
lessons.bodyBn: একবচন -> singular verb; বহুবচন -> plural verb।

lessons.heading: Each / every / either / neither
lessons.body: These are followed by a singular verb.
examples: Each of the boys was present.

lessons.heading: either...or / neither...nor
lessons.body: The verb agrees with the subject NEARER to it.
examples: Neither he nor his friends were there.
Either the boys or the teacher is to blame.

lessons.heading: Tricky subjects
lessons.body: 'A number of' + plural verb; 'The number of' + singular verb. Uncountable nouns and 'each/everyone' take singular.
lessons.bodyBn: A number of -> plural; The number of -> singular।
examples: A number of students are absent.
The number of students is large.

quiz.q: Each of the students ____ a pen.
quiz.explain: 'Each' takes a singular verb -> 'has'.

quiz.q: Neither he nor his brothers ____ present.
quiz.explain: Verb agrees with the nearer subject 'brothers' (plural) -> 'were'.

quiz.q: The number of students ____ increasing.
quiz.explain: 'The number of' takes a singular verb -> 'is'.

quiz.q: A number of people ____ waiting outside.
quiz.explain: 'A number of' takes a plural verb -> 'are'.

quiz.q: Every boy and girl ____ to follow the rules.
quiz.explain: 'Every ... and ...' is treated as singular -> 'has'.

quiz.q: Mathematics ____ my favourite subject.
quiz.explain: 'Mathematics' is singular though it ends in -s -> 'is'.
